Hi Laura,

Thanks for the draft MSA and order form. Our legal team reviewed and attached a set of redlines (Crestwood_Redlines_20261013.docx). A few high-level items we want to confirm before we proceed:

1) Output attribution / ownership — we'd like confirmation that outputs generated by our prompts are owned by Crestwood and that Redwood will not claim title to customer outputs.

2) Training embargo — our default position is a hard opt-out: no model training or use of Customer Content to update models or weights unless we explicitly opt back in. Please confirm how that maps to Redwood's standard feedback license and telemetry clauses.

3) Feedback license — we can provide non-identifiable aggregate telemetry for service quality, but we are not comfortable with a broad perpetual license over prompts/outputs for productization.

Can you point us to proposed language you prefer (MSA vs Order Form) and whether Redwood can accept an Order Form-level checkbox to lock in the training embargo? We are aiming to sign by the end of next week pending alignment.

Best,
Marta Sanchez
Head of Legal, Crestwood Labs

Marta — thanks for the redlines and the clear summary. Appreciate the callout on the three buckets; we can handle these but want to be explicit about operational implications. High level answers below and I've attached a first-pass Redwood proposal redline.

1) Output attribution/ownership — Redwood's standard MSA assigns output rights to the customer with a limited service license to Redwood for operational support (repairs, backups, debugging). We've called that out in Section 5 of our redline (Redwood_proposal_redline.docx). If Crestwood needs an Order Form-level affirmation, we can add an "Output Assignment" clause in the Order Form to make it explicit.

2) Training embargo — we can support a hard opt-out at the Order Form level: we will not use Customer Content to train or update models or weights, period. We do ask for telemetry for safety and platform ops; that can be toggled separately (see below). Language proposed in the redline: "Customer Data will not be used to perform model training, fine-tuning, or weight updates without Customer's prior written consent."

3) Feedback license — propose a narrowly scoped license for aggregated, non-identifiable telemetry strictly for service quality improvements and security (30-day rolling retention by default). No perpetual productization rights over prompt/outputs if you opt-out of training.

Next steps I propose: 1) quick 30-minute sync to agree Order Form checkbox and acceptance path; 2) we incorporate your specific redline text and produce a final redline for routing to procurement/legal; 3) mutual action plan with signature target.

I copied Ben and Priyom to align commercial and evidence items (SLA, telemetry). If that works, Ben — can you propose 2 time slots tomorrow?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Redwood_proposal_redline.docx (docx)
